mostWorthwhile.text: Making the living cell was the strongest moment: the game made the leap from chemistry to life feel consequential while openly acknowledging that its recipe does not explain that leap.

leastWorthwhile.text: Creating dividing cells was a somewhat thin passage: it completed the reproduction goal but gave little detail about reproduction.

surprise.text: Light produced inherited variation rather than the light-using cells I expected. The explanation clarified that variation has several sources and does not arise because organisms need it.

arbitrary.text: The distinction between combining dividing cells with Light and with Sun was unclear beforehand; their different results made sense only after the explanations.

continue.text: Yes. The progression from a cell to shore-building structures was satisfying, and the hint that descendants could change the air gives me a reason to see what happens next.
